title: Portrait and Autopsy
premise: Dominic Blackwood, the unassuming archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, has spent years quietly untangling deaths the police dismissed, hiding her gift behind ledgers and dust. When twin letters arrive—one confessing to a thirty-year-old death in the locked crypt, one promising a fourth 'accident'—she realizes the writer knows her secret and is forcing her into the open. Following alibis woven by the cathedral's oldest families, Dominic discovers the confessing letter was written by a dying man protecting his daughter, while the threatening letter comes from someone who has been watching her for years: her own mentor, the canon, who killed to bury an identity swap that saved his life. In the crypt's final confrontation, Dominic must choose between exposing the truth and preserving the fragile loyalty of the only family she has ever known—and she chooses truth, at the cost of everything she built her invisible life upon.
about_author: Mirabel Almeida is a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing centuries of births, deaths, and quiet scandals before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries from a narrow stone house near the coast, where she insists the best plots are found in archives, not imaginations.

chapters.title: The Weight of Dust
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Establishes her hidden life as cathedral archivist and her private habit of solving 'accidents' the police ignore, including the recent fall of a stonemason from the tower. The emotional beat is controlled loneliness—competence without witness.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Two letters arrive in the same post: one confessing to a death in the sealed crypt thirty years ago, one promising that 'the fourth will be yours.' Dominic realizes the writer knows about her three solved cases. Beat: fear sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Crypt Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. She breaches the locked crypt and finds evidence of a 1994 death ruled a heart attack—a young verger with a fractured skull. The parish register page for that year has been razored out. Beat: dread; the past is curated, not forgotten.

chapters.title: Alibis in Amber
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. She interviews the cathedral's old guard—the sacristan, the organist, the widow of a former dean—each offering flawless, rehearsed alibis for the night of the death. Beat: mounting suspicion that the whole community conspired to forget.

chapters.title: The Dying Confessor
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. She traces the confessing letter to Edmund Voss, a terminally ill former verger who admits writing it—but claims he saw nothing, only signed his name to protect his daughter Clara, who was in the crypt that night. Beat: compassion complicating the hunt.

chapters.title: Clara's Silence
chapters.summary: POV Clara (brief shift). Clara recalls fleeing the crypt in 1994 after finding the verger dead, believing her father did it, and staying silent for thirty years. Present-day Clara warns Dominic to stop digging. Beat: guilt as inheritance.

chapters.title: A Fourth Accident
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The sacristan who helped her into the crypt falls down the tower stairs—alive but broken—and the second letter's promise is fulfilled. Dominic understands she is being punished through proxies. Beat: terror; invisibility offers no protection.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Archives reveal the dead verger had discovered an identity fraud: a seminarian who died abroad was replaced by a survivor who took his name and rose through the Church. Every alibi was built to protect him. Beat: revelation reframing everything.

chapters.title: Vespers in the Dark
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Lured to the crypt during evensong, she confronts Canon Ainsley—the replacement, her mentor, the letter-writer—who argues he has paid for survival every day for thirty years. He offers her complicity; she refuses. Beat: loyalty versus truth at knife-point.

chapters.title: Portrait and Autopsy
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Police arrest Ainsley after Dominic surrenders her anonymous case files as evidence, ending her invisibility deliberately. Clara reconciles with her dying father; Dominic takes down the archivist's portrait of herself she never allowed anyone to paint. Beat: costly, chosen light.
